key_insight: TipSweep transfers learning rates across trainable transformer block counts using precision-dependent scaling: approximately k⁻¹ with FP32 master weights and k⁻¹ᐟ² with direct BF16 updates.
engineering_relevance: Tuning only a small subset of blocks can reduce the memory and compute required to select learning rates for full-model post-training.
method: Search for the best learning rate while training only the last k₀ blocks, typically k₀ = 1.
Predict the learning rate for k trainable blocks by multiplying the tuned rate by (k/k₀)⁻¹ for FP32 master weights or (k/k₀)⁻¹ᐟ² for direct BF16 updates.
Explain the precision-dependent rules with an analytical model accounting for update rounding.
evidence_signal: Experiments span 1–7B-parameter models; 6.7B-model prototypes fit search on a 16 GiB consumer GPU or evaluate five candidate rates using about half the GPU hours of one full-depth run.
watch_item: The scaling rules are approximate and depend on update precision; verify whether training uses FP32 master weights or direct BF16 updates before applying them.
paper_title: Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training
